title: Salsa Morena Magra (Lean Brown Sauce)
description: A sauce made with carrots, onions, and bay leaves.
steps: Place in the bottom of a pot with butter: 5 large carrots sliced lengthwise, 6 large onions sliced, 3 parsley roots, 2 bay leaves, 1 sprig of thyme, 3 cloves, 2 medium carp divided into pieces, 2 medium pike in pieces, salt and pepper
Moisten with 1/2 bottle of white wine and a little lean broth
Let boil and stick to the bottom of the pot until it takes on a dark reddish color
Moisten again with lean broth or in its absence with 1/2 bottle of white wine to deglaze
Remove from heat and mix in 1 pound of butter, sliding it in little by little and stirring always so it does not turn into oil

title: Salsa Rizada Económica (Economical Creamed White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with meat or beef or trimmings or ribs, carrots, and onions.

ingredients.name: Three pounds of scraps or leftovers of meat, such as beef trimmings from the neck, breast, loins, leg, shanks, or ribs, or remains of poultry
A small bunch of parsley and small onions

steps: Place three pounds of meat scraps in a saucepan with some carrots, onions, a small bunch of parsley and small onions, three bay leaves, and three cloves
Add one ladle of water in place of broth and place the saucepan over fairly strong heat
Skim the small amount of broth well, preventing the meat from sticking when the broth has been consumed
Fill the saucepan almost completely with water if broth is not available, adding the necessary salt
Bring the sauce to a boil, skimming it immediately
Place the saucepan on the edge of the stove so the sauce simmers gently for about two hours
When the meat is cooked, strain the broth through a silk sieve
Make a white substance by melting butter in a saucepan and adding as much wheat flour as it can absorb, stirring constantly over the fire without letting it take color until it is well heated
Add mushrooms to this white substance, stirring for ten minutes
Add the broth in which the meat was cooked, being careful that the substance dissolves gradually to prevent lumps from forming
Bring the sauce to a boil, skim it, and place it in a corner of the stove to continue simmering gently for an hour and a half
Remove the fat and pass it through a fine sieve, ensuring it does not take on color, as it is better the whiter it remains

title: Salsa Rizada, Aterciopelada o Apelpada (Creamed White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef, chickens, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Three beef shank bones from the leg of cow
Four onions, one of which studded with two cloves
A large bunch of parsley and small onions
Twenty mushrooms, sautéed cold in water with lemon

steps: Place the beef shanks, chickens, carrots, onions (one studded with cloves), and the bunch of parsley and small onions in a saucepan
Add one tablespoon of concentrated broth and place the saucepan over high heat, taking care to skim the ingredients well
When the broth has reduced, as known by the large bubbles when boiling, add concentrated broth, keeping it well liquid and not allowing it to take on too dark a color
Fill the saucepan with concentrated broth, carefully skimming it well, and when it boils, move it to a corner or edge of the stove
Make a white substance by melting butter in a saucepan and adding wheat flour as much as it can absorb, stirring constantly over the fire without letting it take on color
Add the twenty mushrooms sautéed cold in water with lemon to the white substance, mixing them well with the hot white substance
Dilute this white substance with the small amount of broth from the sauce, then pour it over the ingredients
Let the sauce boil in the corner of the stove, skimming it well, and after an hour and a half, remove the fat
Once the ingredients are cooked, pass the sauce through a fine sieve, ensuring it remains as white as possible
Use the sauce as needed

title: Sopa de la Reina (Queen's Soup)
description: A soup made with fat, ham, and turnips.

ingredients.name: Twelve ounces of lean ham, cut into pieces
A dozen cloves stuck in the onion
A little celery and one garlic clove

steps: Kill the four fat hens the day before they are to be used, clean them well and cook them in a clean pot with the ham, turnips, carrots, onion with cloves, parsley, thyme, bay leaves, celery, and garlic clove.
Add sufficient water and place on the fire, taking great care to skim them, as this considerably depends on the good taste of the soup.
As soon as boiling begins, leave them on a gentle fire, taking care that they cook continuously until they are well cooked.

Remove and let cool, resting on the lower jaw, strip them of their skin and grind the meat on a metate until it becomes a compact paste, moistening it from time to time with a little of the water in which they were cooked.
Pass through a sieve and then take half a pound of very white rice, wash it and half cook it, discard this water and with fresh water cook it again until it is tender.
Grind it the same as the hens, pass through the sieve and mix everything together, add the water in which the hens were cooked, heat well and serve.
The soup will turn out better if you add half a pound of veal leg, as the broth will be stronger. One or two chicken breasts should be set aside to make croquettes and place them in the soup.

title: Sopliros de Monjes (Monks' Puffs)

steps: Put water, a little sugar, a small piece of butter, and lemon zest in a saucepan

Slice half a pound of beef pulp and a piece of ham, doing the same with one onion, some carrots and large turnips
Place this over the fire in a pot and when thick, add some flour and butter
Turn it several times, stirring continuously and add broth, salt, pepper, clove, basil, parsley, onions and bread crusts, being able to add also mushrooms and earth truffles

ingredients.name: Three or four stalks of celery

steps: Place three pounds of beef pulp, three or four old partridges, two pounds of veal shank, one pheasant, carrots, onions, three or four stalks of celery, three cloves, and a small bunch of fennel in a pot or medium marmite and let everything cook together
Roast three young partridges on a spit and after cooling, pound them in a mortar with breadcrumbs three times larger than an egg, soaked in broth
Moisten the pounded mixture with the same broth and, mixing well, pass it through a sieve
Mix the broth of the beef and partridges with this substance so that it is neither too thick nor too liquid

title: Sustancia de Chícharos (Pea Substance)
description: Prepared with peas, onion, and broth.

ingredients.name: One quart to one and a half quarts peas

steps: Soak one quart or quart and a half of peas in water and add four ounces of butter, kneading and working the peas with it
After draining the water, strain them in a colander and put them immediately in a pot placed on a burner that does not have very strong heat
Add a handful of parsley leaves and a little green from onion tops
Fry everything together with the peas, making them jump for a quarter hour

Then add salt and half a ladle of concentrated broth (see concentrated broth, page 131) or pot broth if the other is not available, and let them boil at less heat, taking care to cover the pot with its lid
After three quarters of an hour, remove from the heat and put them in a mortar to pound them
While pounding, pass them through a strainer, using pot broth or cold concentrated broth if available, and keep the substance in a pot
If it is not of a good color, add spinach green (see spinach green, page 322) and heat it at the moment of serving so it does not turn yellowish

title: Sustancia de Garbanzos (Chickpea Substance)
description: Prepared with chickpeas, ham or pork fat, and beef.

ingredients.name: One pound ham or pork fat
One and a half pounds beef pulp

steps: Wash one quart of chickpeas and put them in a medium pot with one pound of ham or pork fat, one and a half pounds of beef pulp, two or three carrots and the same number of onions, one of which should be studded with two cloves of spice
Fill the pot almost entirely with broth and let the chickpeas cook
When done, put them in a strainer, let them drain and dry, and remove the ham, beef and vegetables

Pass the chickpeas through the strainer, moistening them little by little with broth from the same pot in which they were cooked, making the substance thick, as it is easier to liquefy than to thicken afterwards
Put it in a pot with four skimming spoonfuls of skimmed sauce (see page 766)
After boiling and skimming, degrease it
When sufficiently thick, empty it into another pot, and at the moment of serving, mix in spinach green (see page 322)

Put the beans in it and moisten them with broth or water

steps: After washing one and a half quarts of lentils, put them in a pot with one pound of pork fat, one and a half pounds of beef pulp, two carrots and three onions, one of which is studded with two cloves of spice
Fill the pot with broth and let the lentils cook
When done, remove the vegetables, fat and beef, and pass them through a strainer
When the broth has been wrung out, put the substance in a pot with four skimming spoonfuls of Spanish sauce (see page 795)
More broth is needed in this substance than in that of chickpeas, because it is necessary for it to boil a long time to take color, taking care to skim and degrease it

title: Sustancia de Zanahorias (Carrot Substance)
description: Prepared with carrots, onions, and broth.
steps: Cut thirty well-cleaned carrots lengthwise into slices and place in a saucepan with half a pound of butter and seven or eight onions cut into quarters, after having removed the stems and roots
When the butter has melted, fry the carrots, taking care to stir them so they do not stick
When slightly fried, moisten with broth, adding a small piece of sugar the size of a walnut
After having been allowed to cook over gentle heat for three hours, check if they fall apart easily when pressed gently between the fingers
Remove the substance from the heat and pour it into a sieve through which it will be passed, having removed the broth and pounded the roots

To strain it easily, moisten it from time to time with the same broth in which the carrots were cooked, being necessary that it remain quite liquid and that it does not boil for long if you want it not to turn bitter

Once the substance is in the saucepan, add four tablespoons of curled sauce, and if any broth from the carrots remains, add it to the substance, then let it reduce sufficiently, skimming and degreasing it, until it becomes so thick that it can cover the entrees for which it was prepared

description: Prepared with egg yolks, yeast, and broth.
steps: Mix flour with 4 egg yolks and one cup of warm water, stirring well and seasoning with fine salt while kneading, adding a small piece of yeast.

title: Tamal de Castilla al Estilo de Veracruz (Veracruz-Style Pork Tamal)
description: Prepared with corn, broth, and lard.

ingredients.name: one real of masa (corn dough) for tortillas
broth from two reals of pork meat mixed with ears and ribs
one hoja santa or epazote leaf
three types of chiles: ancho, pasilla, and mulato (one tlaco of each)
pieces of hoja santa or epazote

steps: Mix the masa with the broth where the pork has been cooked, season with sufficient salt and add six ounces of lard
Cook while stirring constantly so it does not stick
Test the masa and when cooked, remove it; the consistency should be slightly thicker than ponche
Add one hoja santa or epazote leaf to the masa
Take three types of chiles, one tlaco of each (ancho, pasilla, and mulato), remove veins and toast them very well, then grind
Fry eight to ten tomatoes in lard, then grind and combine with the chile
Fry well and add the meat and a little of its broth, with pieces of hoja santa or epazote
In a large casserole greased with much lard, layer the masa, then meat and mole, alternating until finished, ensuring the last layer is masa
Leave some mole without meat to place on top
Place on a well-heated burner with a comal with fire on top
Insert a popote (straw) to test; when it comes out clean, it is done
Remove and let rest all night
In the morning, reheat in the same manner; if made during the day, do so very early so it can rest

title: Tamales (Corn Tamales)
description: Prepared with corn, lard, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: One pound four ounces of lard
One cup of strong tequesquite water

steps: Prepare seven cups of corn as nixtamal.
The next day, wash and dry in the sun.
Once dry, grind and sift through an ayate.
In a cazuela, place one pound four ounces of lard, six egg yolks, and beat together with a spoon.
Once well beaten, incorporate the corn.
Add one cup of strong tequesquite water and if the masa becomes thick, add pure water and salt to taste.
Let rest for two or more hours and beat well.
Make mole with pork that is thick and mix with the masa.
In a pot, make a tapextle with sticks and leaves and add water so it does not overflow the sticks.
Place the tamales on this base and cover with leaves and cloth so the pot is well sealed.
Cook over regular heat.
For sweet tamales, fill with custard instead. The same operation can be done with rice.

title: Tamales Cernidos de Maíz Cacahuatzentli (Sifted Cacahuatzentli Corn Tamales)
description: Prepared with corn, lard, and salt or sugar.

ingredients.name: three pounds or slightly more of lard

steps: Make nixtamal or cook three pounds of cacahuatzentli corn the same way as for common tamales
Wash it well, dry it and put it to dry in the sun
When completely dry, grind it, and then sift it through a thin ayate cloth
To the sifted portion add three pounds or slightly more of lard and a little warm water

Beat this mass with the necessary salt, or if you want to make it sweet, with sugar, beating until it makes eyes and is at the right point, which you will know by forming a small ball from it that when dropped in water floats
Form the tamales in corn husks, making sure these have well drained the water in which they were soaked, and once made, put them to cook the same way as in the previous article
If you do not want to make them sweet, do not add sugar to the mass, but season well with salt, and fill the tamales with the stews you want made of meat or fish, chile or spice
If they are sweet, they can be filled with cooked egg yolks, ground sugar, pine nuts, citron, cinnamon and sesame

title: Tamales Cominos ó Cernido de Maíz Común (Tamales of Ground Common Corn)
description: Prepared with corn, white sugar, and lard.
steps: Prepare the corn as for nixtamal and remove the hull
Wash and grind entirely as if for atole
Once well ground, pass the dough through an ayate cloth
After sifting, mix nine ounces of white sugar and one pound of lard with corresponding fine salt and a little anise
Moisten the dough with warm water and beat well
Place quantities of the dough on washed, soaked, drained and dried corn leaves
Wrap and cover with them, fold in half, and form the tamales
Put a pot of sufficient capacity on the heat with very little water, optionally placing a little grass in the water to control the boil
Form a wooden grate above it and arrange the tamales so the water does not reach them and they cook only by steam
Cover the pot opening with a cazuela of its size and a cloth tied very well
When the dough detaches from the leaf it is a sign they are cooked
Remove from heat and serve hot, alone or with milk atole

title: Tamales Comunes, o Cernidos de Maíz Común (Common or Sifted Corn Tamales)
description: Prepared with corn, white sugar, and lard.

ingredients.name: nine and a half ounces of white sugar
corn husks, washed, soaked, drained, and dried

steps: Prepare the corn as nixtamal, remove the husks, wash it and grind it completely the same way as for making atole

Once the mass is well ground, pass it through a cloth or ayate, and after sifting, mix nine and a half ounces of white sugar and one pound of lard with the corresponding fine salt and a little anise, moistening the mass as needed with warm water

Beat it well, and on washed corn husks that have been soaked, drained, and dried, place the quantities of mass that they can hold, wrapping and covering with them, and folding in half to form the tamales

Put a pot of sufficient capacity on the fire with very little water; you can put a little grass inside this water to stop the boiling; above this, form a small lattice or framework of wooden strips, and arrange the tamales so that the water does not reach them, cooking them only by steam
Cover the mouth of the pot with a bowl of its size and a cloth that is tied well

title: Tamales de Arroz (Rice Tamales)

title: Tamales de Arroz (Rice Tamales)
description: Prepared with rice, egg yolks, and corn.

ingredients.name: manjar blanco (dulce de leche) or yellow milk

steps: Wash the rice very well, spread it on a napkin and place it in the sun
Once it is completely dry, grind it very finely and pass it through a sieve
In a bowl where it can be beaten well, gradually add melted and clarified butter
Add finely ground sugar and beat until the sweet paste is very thick, as it will thin during cooking
Once sweetened, add an amount of milk equal to the amount of water used, and one or two egg yolks
The milk should be lukewarm so the paste does not become hard
Add a little salt and continue beating until the batter makes an eye or the spoon stands alone in the middle of the paste
Paint the corn husks with red and yellow stripes made with bread crumbs and yellow milk with egg yolks respectively
Place the tamales in the husks with a spoon and fill them with raisins, almonds, or manjar blanco or yellow milk
Cook them and do not unwrap until they are cold, or they will fall apart

Continue beating, and when it begins to set, add powdered sugar to taste.
Beat it more until it reaches the proper point, which is known when a small piece of the masa floats on water.
Form the tamales in well-drained corn husks and they can be filled with any milk-based or fruit dessert.

half a pound of pasilla chiles
about a handful or slightly less of cilantro
half a quarter-liter of cooked tomatoes
half a head of roasted garlic

steps: Toast in lard half a pound of ancho chiles and another half pound of pasillas, taking care that they do not burn
Toast also in the lard about a handful or slightly less of cilantro
Grind both things together with half a quarter-liter of cooked tomatoes, half a head of roasted garlic and some pepper, clove and toasted sesame seeds

Pass through cheesecloth as a substance

description: A bread preparation made with sweet potato, milk, and almond.

ingredients.name: six egg yolks per pound of sugar
four ounces of ground almond per pound of sweet potato

steps: Mix ground sweet potato with sugar in equal proportion and two gourds of milk for each pound of sugar
Cook over heat and before reaching medium consistency, add six well-beaten egg yolks per pound of sugar, adding one at a time while stirring the paste quickly so it does not stick
Add four ounces of ground almond per pound of sweet potato, dissolved in a little orange flower water
Cook to a point slightly lower than cajeta, then remove from heat and pour onto a plate to rest until the next day
Meanwhile, boil two or three pounds of sugar with water according to the quantity of fried bread needed

Clarify and when the syrup reaches medium consistency, remove from heat and add cinnamon, a little clove, a quarter or less of white wine, raisins, almonds, pine nuts, toasted sesame seeds and orange flower water; set aside until the next day
Cut bread slices carefully so they do not fall apart
Mix with the paste made the previous day, raisins, almonds, pine nuts and sesame seeds
Place a little of this mixture on each slice and cover with its companion slice
Take each fried bread carefully in hand and coat vigorously with beaten egg that has been prepared with the yolks and whites beaten separately
Fry in lard of regular temperature (if too cold the fried breads will become greasy, if too hot they will burn)
Remove from lard and place where they can drain
When serving, pour syrup with gragea and ground cinnamon over them

title: Torta al Natural (Plain Omelet)
description: Prepared with eggs, water, and salt.
steps: Beat some eggs according to the size of the omelet, and add half or one spoonful of fresh water, which greatly facilitates the intimate mixing of the whites and yolks
Season with fine salt mixed with a little pepper
Melt fresh butter in a pan, pour the beaten eggs into it and stir until the omelet begins to set
When it is set, lift it with the point of a knife and put another amount of fresh butter underneath
As soon as it has melted, turn the omelet by folding it over itself, which is done easily, leave it one or two minutes in the pan and place it on a platter to serve immediately

The flavor of the plain omelet can be varied infinitely by adding to the eggs, at the moment of beating them, grated cheese, minced fine herbs, cooked sorrel, sauce or meat juice; the procedure does not change in any of these cases

Butter a pan and add the batter

title: Torta de Almendra en Grande o para Casas de Comunidad (Large Almond Cake or for Community Houses)
description: A cake made with ground almonds, egg white, and biscuit.

ingredients.name: Eight pounds of blanched and ground almonds
Egg white and lemon for clarification
Dough for the base as described in the following article

steps: Make a syrup with one arroba of sugar, clarified with egg white and lemon, then skim it
Add the almonds ground and not too whole into the syrup and let it boil until it reaches the mirror point, stirring constantly so it does not burn
Store for another day
When ready to put into the cake pans, add a little ground biscuit, a little white honey, and as many egg yolks as desired
Prepare the cake pans two or three days in advance, light the oven, and once it is reduced to embers, place the pans with abundant cold lard on top
Put a base of dough like that described in the following article, not too thick nor too thin, and once the base is slightly cool, put the border which will adhere to the base so they do not separate
The oven must burn for two or three hours and rest for as many more; it must be well heated and very calm
When the oven is at embers, put the paste in the pans without filling them so they do not spill
Extend the dough of the same as the bases, though thinner, and with a pastry wheel cut strips less than a finger's width
Wet the border and put it in small latticed strips rolled up, sprinkling sesame seeds on top

Put the pans into the oven, swept without water, testing with one; if it boils very briefly, the others should not yet be put in so they do not spill, and let rest a little more until it is of good temperament
Once golden, remove from the oven

Place one sheet of this dough in a casserole greased with butter

description: A cake made with cheese, cinnamon, and almonds.

ingredients.name: 4 ounces of soaked almonds, not very finely ground
half a pound of melted and cooled butter
half a pound of fresh cheese, ground
12 eggs, beaten and well risen, whites and yolks separated
1 pound and a half of sugar
raisins, almonds, pine nuts, and candied citron

steps: Mix well the soaked almonds, sifted sugar, melted and cooled butter, ground fresh cheese, well-risen beaten eggs with whites and yolks separated, and cinnamon powder in sufficient quantity to give the cake the desired color
When everything is well incorporated and no lumps of almond remain, pour the batter onto one or two sheets of buttered paper prepared in a buttered pan
Bake at two gentle fires until set
When cooked, remove the cake from the pan with the same papers and drain any remaining butter
Carefully replace the cake, removing the papers
Pierce it with a popote (reed or straw) all the way through to the bottom
Pour clarified syrup at medium point made with a pound and a half of sugar over it
Simmer gently until the syrup is consumed and the cake is dry
Serve studded with raisins, almonds, pine nuts, and candied citron
It can also be made without syrup, using instead sifted sugar and two ounces of toasted and ground sponge cake
Both versions can have a crust made with biscuit, sugar, cinnamon, and butter
